findings.explanation: Get-VsanRuntimeInfo is a cluster-scoped cmdlet that takes -Cluster. It does not accept VMHost objects from the pipeline and does not return a per-host used-capacity property. The documented way to source 'largest host contribution' therefore does not work, and the safe_to_evacuate_one_host gate has no valid input.
findings.suggested_fix: Source per-host vSAN used capacity from a supported path, such as per-disk or disk-group capacity summed by host from the vSAN API or Get-VsanDisk with capacity details. Name the exact cmdlet or API and property after checking the PowerCLI reference.

findings.explanation: No such add-on exists. Splunkbase 5380, cited for it in references, detailedImplementation and implementation, is 'Mattermost Alerts'. The real add-on is the Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215, splunk_TA_vmware), and it emits vmware:events and vmware:perf:* sourcetypes, not vmware:vc:event or a bare vmware:perf. The Tertiary and Appendix H drill guidance points at an app and sourcetypes that do not exist.
findings.quote: (optional) Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere Forwarder
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215)' and use vmware:events and vmware:perf:datastore or vmware:perf:disk for the drill panels in app, implementation, visualization, references and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: Binary and decimal units differ by about 7.4% at GiB versus GB and about 10% at TiB versus TB, not 1–2%. The PowerCLI docs also state that Get-VsanSpaceUsage 'GB' attributes are already GiB. Operators following this text would either accept real discrepancies or misattribute a unit gap.
findings.quote: Differences in tebibyte versus gigabyte are expected at one to two percent; log both units in the evidence pack.
findings.suggested_fix: State that PowerCLI '...GB' values are GiB (base 2). Compare against the vSphere client in the same unit, and expect about 7% (GiB vs GB) or about 10% (TiB vs TB) when units differ.

findings.explanation: The sample capacity line does not match the search in three ways. It puts the largest-host value on vmware:vsan:capacity as largestHostContributionGB, but the search only reads largest_host_contribution_gb from the separate vmware:vsan:host_runtime join. It emits no host_failures_to_tolerate and no slack field. Its cluster_id is the vCenter MoRef (for example ClusterComputeResource-domain-c8), while the VxRail join expects the VxRail Manager cluster_id. Following the sample yields null storm estimates, an FTT of 0 and failed VxRail joins.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the sample emit exactly what the search reads: a host_runtime line with per_host_contribution_gb, an FTT field and a slack field. Define one canonical cluster_id, and say how the VxRail cluster ID maps to the vCenter cluster MoRef, for example via the lookup.

findings.explanation: A host's vSAN used capacity already includes the replica or parity components it stores. A full-data-migration evacuation needs roughly that host's used capacity free elsewhere, not that amount multiplied by FTT+1. The multiplier overstates the requirement by 2–3x, so healthy clusters are reported as 'no' and the gate becomes unusable. Appendix E calls it a 'planning multiplier' but never justifies the factor.
findings.quote: The inequality safe_to_evacuate_one_host uses the storm estimate of largest times (ftt+1).
findings.suggested_fix: Base the estimate on the largest host's used capacity plus the operations reserve and slack, or on the vSphere data-migration pre-check result. Document why any extra multiplier exists, with a VMware sizing reference.

findings.explanation: When the policy feed and the capacity-line FTT are missing, coalesce defaults ftt_src to "0" and ftt_policy to "0". Those values are non-null, so ftt_use becomes 0, not 1, and the '"1"' fallback in ftt_use is unreachable. The troubleshooting tip describes the wrong symptom.
findings.quote: (9) ftt always 1: storage_policy feed may be empty; add policy export.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that an empty policy feed shows ftt_use=0, and tell operators to set ftt_required in the lookup.

findings.explanation: No Dell OpenManage add-on appears in the cached Splunkbase catalogue; the Dell entries are PowerMax, ECS and AIOps only. detailedImplementation also says no Splunkbase app ships the VxRail contract. Calling it PRIMARY without a Splunkbase ID or vendor link is unsupported, and contradicts the custom-HEC framing.
findings.quote: PRIMARY: Dell EMC OpenManage Splunk Add-on when deployed for VxRail
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Splunkbase ID or Dell download URL for the add-on, or remove it and make the custom VxRail Manager HEC poller the stated primary path.

findings.explanation: Catalogue-authoring meta text has leaked into customer-facing guidance. Appendices D, F and G largely repeat earlier content (the CSV governance, the ftt coalesce caveat, the seven-column contract) and add length without new operational facts.
findings.quote: Avoid marketing language in your internal wiki; the forbidden-phrase list in the authoring contract applies. ... This appendix brings the hand-authored portion together with the five steps. If a future schema asks for a shorter detailedImplementation, split appendices to a private runbook
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the authoring-contract sentences. Collapse Appendices D, F and G into one short governance note, or remove them.

findings.explanation: RVC is deprecated in current vCenter releases, and 'read-only RVC' is not a mode it offers. The vSphere client's vSAN data-migration pre-check is the supported equivalent and is mentioned only in passing.
findings.quote: Run RVC on a vCenter with read-only RVC, vsan.whatif_host_failures, capture output for CAB
findings.suggested_fix: Make the vSphere client data-migration pre-check (Monitor > vSAN) the primary validation step, and note RVC only for legacy vCenter versions where it is still available.

findings.explanation: Step 2 says 'Earliest: -6h; latest: @h', while implementation and the search use -6h@h. The PowerCLI export runs every 30 minutes, but Step 1 schedules the VxRail poller 'every five minutes on cron', so the cadence story is inconsistent across fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one window, earliest=-6h@h latest=@h, in all fields, and one stated cadence per feed.

findings.explanation: VxRail is a Dell-engineered appliance line, not vSAN ReadyNode hardware. Exclusions explicitly send ReadyNode deployments to UC-19.2.2 and UC-19.2.27, so this clause contradicts the scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the ReadyNode phrase; keep the VxRail series and PowerEdge generation list.

findings.explanation: Cisco ACI has no role in VxRail vSAN capacity, and the equipment tags 'cisco' and 'hardware_bmc' are likewise unrelated to the REST and PowerCLI data path.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove cisco_aci, cisco and hardware_bmc; keep vxrail, dell_emc, vmware, vmware_vcenter and vmware_vsphere.

findings.explanation: The HEC reference is truncated to the Data manual root. The 5380 reference points to an unrelated app, and there is no reference for Get-VsanSpaceUsage or the VxRail API paths the UC depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/Data/UsetheHEC, replace 5380 with https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3215, and add the Get-VsanSpaceUsage PowerCLI reference page.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by a generic handle, but the core per-host input cmdlet does not work as written, the drill add-on is misidentified, and the sample poller does not feed the search's fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade to draft until a named reviewer has run the export and search on a real VxRail cluster.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The 'critical' branch requires slack_pct<tmins, but slack_pct is null whenever slack is not exported, because coalesce defaults it to "0" and slack_pct is only set when slack>0. Get-VsanSpaceUsage and the documented sample emit no slack field, so 'critical' is unreachable in the documented collection path.

ftt_src and ftt_policy default to "0" through coalesce, so ftt_use falls to 0 rather than the intended "1" fallback when the feeds are missing. The evacuation estimate then uses (0+1), which understates the requirement.

'sort 0 + severity0' sorts alphabetically (critical, high, low, medium, ok), so low ranks above medium. The freeze rewrites even 'critical' to 'info' for severity_bucket. largest_host_contribution_gb is read only from the host_runtime join, not from the capacity line where the documented sample puts it.

summary: The UC clearly separates itself from its siblings and is careful about ESA and stretched-cluster exclusions. However, its collection recipe relies on a per-host Get-VsanRuntimeInfo pipe that does not exist, a misidentified Splunkbase 5380 add-on with sourcetypes the real VMware add-on does not emit, and a GiB-versus-GB reconciliation claim the PowerCLI docs contradict. The PowerShell sample also does not produce the fields and join keys the search expects, and the appendices contain authoring-meta filler.
